card.name: Danza (Cuba)
card.profile: The Cuban danza was an early-19th-century creole ballroom dance and music form - a derivative of the contradanza (contradanza criolla / danza criolla / habanera). The oldest known Cuban danza, 'El Sungambelo,' dates to 1813. Unlike the figure-based contradanza, the danza introduced the closed couple-hold (influenced by the waltz), with slower, more relaxed movements and the characteristic habanera rhythm. It is a direct ancestor of the danzon (1879, Miguel Failde) and thus of mambo and cha-cha-cha (English Wikipedia: Contradanza; Peter Manuel, CUNY).
card.insight: Per musicologist Argeliers Leon, the danza was musically near-identical to the contradanza but danced differently, marking the Cuban transition from communal sequence dances to independent couple dances (English Wikipedia: Contradanza).
